messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Signs of an allergic reaction to prednisone include difficult breathing.
Signs of an allergic reaction to prednisone include swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
signs of infection, such as fever, chills, sore throat, cough or a wound that is not healing, since prednisone can hide the usual warning signs;
blurred vision, eye pain or seeing halos around lights, which can be signs of glaucoma (raised pressure in the eye) or cataracts;
You have severe pain in your upper stomach.
The pain spreads to your back.
You experience nausea.
You experience vomiting.
These symptoms can be a sign of pancreatitis.
Pancreatitis is an inflamed pancreas.
bloody or black, tarry stools, or vomit that looks like coffee grounds, which can be signs of a bleeding stomach ulcer;
severe depression, unusual excitement, confusion, changes in personality or behavior, or a seizure;
swelling, rapid weight gain or shortness of breath, which can be signs of fluid retention or heart failure;
Triplet: ["severe pain in upper stomach", "can indicate", "pancreatitis"]

The relation 'can indicate' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject entity may be a sign or symptom of the medical condition specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'may indicate': The subject condition or symptom may be a sign or indicator of the medical condition specified by the object entity.
B. 'has symptom': The condition specified by the subject entity is associated with the symptom specified by the object entity.
C. 'mimics': The subject condition or symptom is similar to or can be mistaken for the condition or symptom specified by the object entity.
D. 'have': The subject group of patients has the medical condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
E. 'known as': The subject medical condition is also referred to by the name specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
